grandparents_cupboard.reason: Oats, oil, golden syrup, brown sugar, pumpkin seeds and fresh figs are all plain home staples with no factory-made products.

supermarket.reason: Fresh figs, pumpkin seeds and the rest are sold at Tesco in August at ordinary prices.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a small pan, a square baking dish and baking paper, using simple melt-stir-press technique.

works.reason: The oats, fat and syrup are in workable flapjack proportions for a 20cm dish, with a sensible 25 minute bake at 180°C that gives 12 bars.

honest_times.reason: 15 minutes covers melting, chopping six figs and pressing, and the 55 cook minutes match the 25 minute bake plus 30 minutes cooling.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Fresh figs are mixed through and laid on top of an early August bake, so they are clearly the point of it.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British home-cook instructions with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Oat, seed and fresh fig bars make a sensible, filling family snack rather than mostly sugar.
